title: 7 mental models that make hard decisions easier
intro_line: A mental model is just a reliable way of seeing a problem. Collect enough of them and fewer decisions feel hard.

items.name: Inversion
items.explanation: Instead of asking how to succeed, ask how to fail — then avoid that. Charlie Munger built a fortune mostly by not being stupid.

items.name: Opportunity cost
items.explanation: Every yes is a no to everything else you could do with that time or money. The real cost of a choice is the best thing you gave up.

items.name: Second-order thinking
items.explanation: Ask 'and then what?' A cheap decision today can be expensive in six months. Play the tape forward.

items.name: Circle of competence
items.explanation: Know the edge of what you actually understand, and be honest about it. Most big mistakes happen just outside that line.

items.name: Occam's razor
items.explanation: When explanations compete, the simplest that fits is usually right. Complexity is often a place to hide.

items.name: Margin of safety
items.explanation: Leave room for being wrong. Build the bridge to hold more than the heaviest truck you expect.

items.name: Confirmation bias
items.explanation: You find what you look for. Actively hunt for the evidence you'd rather not see before you commit.

closing_line: You don't need to be smarter than everyone. You just need a few good models and the discipline to actually use them.

title: 5 habits that quietly compound over a decade
intro_line: None of these change your week. All of them change your decade.

items.name: Read 20 pages a day
items.explanation: That's about 20-30 books a year. In ten years you've read more than most people do in a lifetime.

items.name: Automate one good decision
items.explanation: Save before you see the paycheck; lay tomorrow's clothes out tonight. Willpower is fragile; defaults aren't.

items.name: Walk every day
items.explanation: Not a workout — a walk. It's the most underrated tool for thinking clearly and staying steady.

items.name: Write things down
items.explanation: A short daily note turns a vague life into a reviewable one. What gets tracked gets understood.

items.name: Sleep like it's your job
items.explanation: Almost every skill you care about — focus, patience, memory, mood — is downstream of rest.

closing_line: Boring, repeated, and undisturbed beats impressive and inconsistent. Pick one and start tonight.
